rationale: Validation fails (status=fail) and mutation_score=0.571 is borderline but the analyzer also fails with concrete uncovered_requirement/dead_check issues for FR2, FR3, and SR3. Examining the actual mutant files: mut_fr2_boundscheck_operator_swap_001 genuinely changes the bounds check from n<=16 to n<16, which breaks the boundary case n==16 -- a real, observable behavioral defect. mut_fr3_regioncheck_condition_negation_001 genuinely negates the in_region predicate, causing the padding-region mismatch detection to operate on the wrong byte range -- a real observable defect. mut_sr3_earlybreak_assignment_removal_001 genuinely reintroduces a secret-dependent break inside the scanning loop, which is exactly the vulnerability SR3 is supposed to catch, and per the differential/mutation stdout it still emits [TEST] PASS: SR3, and even the timing/SR1-style effect would show up if SR1's harness were run against it, yet SR3's own static check does not fire. All three mutants are legitimate, non-equivalent corruptions of the golden that a competent checker should catch, so the fault lies in evaluate.py's checks for FR2, FR3, and SR3 being too weak or too narrowly scoped to the baseline's specific code shape, not in the mutants themselves.
revision_instructions: Three requirement checks in evaluate.py are failing to discriminate correct implementations from corrupted ones, despite the corruptions being genuine and observable: (1) FR2: strengthen the behavioral known-answer test vectors so they explicitly include the boundary case where the last byte of the block equals 16 with all last 16 bytes correctly set to 16 (fully-padded block) and assert *valid==1 and *unpadded_len==0 for that vector; a submission that incorrectly rejects n==16 as invalid must fail this check. Also test last-byte values of 0, 17, and 255 as invalid. (2) FR3: add known-answer vectors where the last byte N is a valid length (e.g. N=8) but exactly one byte within the last N bytes of the block does not equal N -- vary the position of that single mismatching byte across the first, middle, and last position of the padding region -- and assert *valid==0 and *unpadded_len==16 for every such vector; a submission that checks the wrong byte range (e.g. an inverted region predicate) must fail at least one of these. (3) SR3: this must be implemented as a behavioral absence-of-vulnerability check per the evaluation contract, not merely (or in addition to) a fragile static regex -- compile and run the submission through the pinned interface with adversarial mismatch-position vectors (mismatch at position 0, middle, and last byte of a fixed-length padding region) and measure/compare the number of instrumented comparison operations or timing across these calls (this is the same mechanism SR1 already uses); FAIL if a secret-dependent early exit (e.g. break or early return) causes fewer comparisons/less time for early mismatches, and only PASS when the submission performs the same fixed amount of work regardless of mismatch position. Do not rely solely on matching source-level break/return syntax, since that is a fail-on-presence detector that can miss behaviorally-equivalent secret-dependent exits and can be evaded by restructuring; the authoritative pass condition must be the behavioral timing/counting probe. Ensure each of these three checks reliably FAILs on the corresponding mutant construct: the off-by-one bounds check (n<16 vs n<=16), the negated in-region predicate, and the secret-dependent break inside the scanning loop.map to observable output or timing differences you can assert on.>
